findings.reason: §2/§3 would have to state the accepted-directory exception, or the plan would extend the directory-claim owner rather than only the generic predicate, and either edit changes the authored rule.
findings.text: the plan pins its topic-directory rule only against `_scopes_overlap`, but a declared directory overlapping a live claim is judged by the separate `_directory_claim_overlaps` arm and refused as `DirectoryClaimConflict` (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:147), which a caller avoids with `--accept-directory-claim` (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:2774-2805); so §3's absolute "beneath docs/figures/ is claimed by exactly one node ... not a shared workspace" is escapable — a node declaring a directory inside a claimed topic proceeds with the flag (demonstrated by tests/test_directory_claim_asks_first.py::test_the_flag_lets_an_absent_directory_claim_proceed)

findings.reason: the §1 premise and §3's "exactly one node" phrasing must acknowledge the existing per-node figure-directory grant, which is the closest prior art and the reason sibling writers beneath one figure tree are already admitted.
findings.text: §1 asserts "Nothing states the allocation unit", but dispatch already allocates figure space per node as the granted landing scope `docs/figures/<plan>/<node-id>/` (`_granted_landing_paths`, reckon/crew/dispatch.py:2044-2047), so two nodes on one plan already hold disjoint scopes beneath a single `docs/figures/<plan>/` topic by default (tests/test_crew_dispatch_guard.py::test_two_concurrent_nodes_each_hold_their_own_landing_fragment)

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — no new module is proposed; §2 is a six-line mechanism comment (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:7055) plus tests over the existing guard, so there is no new interface to weigh for depth.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the plan extends the existing dispatch guard and the existing scope-claim readers (`runs._live_scope_claims`, `runs.scope_claims` at reckon/crew/runs.py:769,819) rather than forking placement, path resolution or claim storage; the owners are untouched and remain single.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites only the generic containment predicate `_scopes_overlap` (reckon/crew/runs.py:693) and does not cite dispatch's dedicated directory-claim mechanism (`_directory_claim_overlaps`, `DirectoryClaimConflict`, `--accept-directory-claim`) nor its per-node figure-directory grant, both of which already govern the space the §3 rule describes.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §3 adds no layer over machinery; it extends the two documentation surfaces that already carry figure guidance rather than introducing a parallel mechanism.
